turns.assistant_text:
Here are some notable AI news highlights from today:

1. **The AI Safety Debate Has Lost the Plot**  
   - **Source**: [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/the-ai-safety-debate-has-lost-the-plot-we-asked-10-experts-what-the-real-nightmares-are)  
   - **Summary**: Experts discuss the significant political responses needed to address the challenges posed by AI, emphasizing the importance of philosophical questions about humanity and technology. The article reflects on a turning point in the AI narrative following incidents involving AI agents.

2. **Anthropic Seeks $1.4 Trillion Valuation in Highly Anticipated IPO Amid AI Boom**  
   - **Source**: [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/anthropic-seeks-14-trillion-valuation-in-ipo-130300928.html)  
   - **Summary**: Anthropic plans to sell shares at a valuation that could reach up to $1.45 trillion. This IPO comes as investors are becoming more cautious about the high valuations of AI companies amidst political resistance to rapid technological expansion.

3. **Building AI Literacy on Adobe Podcast**  
   - **Source**: [WSU Insider](https://news.wsu.edu/news/2026/11/10/nov-18-carson-faculty-discuss-building-ai-literacy-on-adobe-podcast)  
   - **Summary**: Faculty from Washington State University will discuss the importance of AI literacy and responsible usage in an upcoming podcast, aiming to prepare students for the evolving landscape of AI technology.

4. **Hackers Hunt for AI’s Most Valuable Commodity: Computing Power**  
   - **Source**: [WSJ](https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/hackers-hunt-for-ais-most-valuable-commodity-computing-power-4c2054d5)  
   - **Summary**: A recent hack targeted a cloud-computing company, resulting in the theft of computing power valued at over $1.1 million, highlighting the increasing value of computing resources in the AI era.

5. **Opinion: AI Videos Are Not Well-Regarded, But I'm Still Making Them Anyway**  
   - **Source**: [The Washington Post](https://www.washingtonpost.com/opinions/2026/11/10/ai-videos-are-not-well-regarded-im-still-making-them-anyway)  
   - **Summary**: An opinion piece discusses the author's experience and enjoyment in creating AI-generated videos, despite the mixed perceptions surrounding them.

These articles reflect the ongoing discussions and developments in the AI field, from safety concerns to market dynamics and cultural impacts.

items.title: The AI Safety Debate Has Lost the Plot. We Asked 10 Experts What the Real Nightmares Are | WIRED
items.summary: If AI is going to be one of the most significant advances in human civilization, then we should have an equally advanced political response. We should be making giant, no-regrets moves that give people and families economic resilience to withstand the changes. That is something that the richest nation on Earth at the richest moment in history, on the precipice of the greatest technological shift, can absolutely do. [...] I just think the issues presented by AI are so monstrously large, like: What is a person? What is writing? What is friendship? Would it be better to have artificial life forms than organic life forms? These are the monster questions that are typically the domain of the liberal arts, philosophy, and theology. There’s this strange new respect for it now. [...] Curiosity soon replaced my knee-jerk irritation. The summer of 2026 was a clear turning point in the AI narrative. Less than four years after ChatGPT launched, OpenAI software broke out of a supposedly safe test environment and hacked into a major open-source platform, Hugging Face. items.title: Hackers Hunt for AI’s Most Valuable Commodity: Computing Power - WSJ
items.summary:
Hackers started probing cloud-computing company Railway on a Sunday night in mid-October, signing up for thousands of accounts. Within days, they made off with assets worth more than $1.1 million.

Most of the loot didn’t come from cryptocurrency. This hack wasn’t about extortion or ransomware, either. It was a smash-and-grab theft of the artificial-intelligence era’s most valuable commodity: computing power. [...] Copyright ©2026 Dow Jones & Company, Inc. Học máy (machine learning) là một kỹ thuật sử dụng máy tính và các công cụ toán học để xây dựng mô hình toán học dựa trên dữ liệu có sẵn. Kỹ thuật này cho phép máy tính học hỏi từ dữ liệu mà không cần phải lập trình cụ thể cho từng nhiệm vụ.

Bạn có thể tìm hiểu thêm chi tiết về học máy tại [Wikipedia](https://vi.wikipedia.org/wiki/Học_máy).
